subject: Maths
title: Estimating calculations
subtitle: Place Value and Ordering Integers · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can estimate answers to calculations by rounding numbers to one significant figure.

key_vocab.definition: To estimate a calculation, round each number to one significant figure (1 s.f.) first, then perform the calculation with the rounded values.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can estimate answers to calculations by rounding numbers to one significant figure.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Estimating calculations -- To estimate a calculation, round each number to one significant figure (1 s.f.) first, then perform the calculation with the rounded values.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Round every number to 1 significant figure, then calculate. The symbol ≈ means approximately equal to.
3.8 × 19.6 ≈ 4 × 20 = 80
Round each value to 1 s.f. before calculating

Key examples:
  ✓ 48 × 31 ≈ 50 × 30 = 1500  (round to 1 s.f.)
  ✓ 198 ÷ 4.1 ≈ 200 ÷ 4 = 50  (round each number)
  ✓ √26 ≈ √25 = 5  (round to nearest square)
  ✗ 48 × 31 ≈ 48 × 30 = 1440  (must round both numbers)
  ✗ 3.7 rounded to 1 s.f. is 3  (should be 4)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – multiplication estimate
  Estimate 38 × 52
  Round: 38 ≈ 40, 52 ≈ 50
  40 × 50
  = 2000
  ≈ 2000
  (Both numbers rounded to 1 significant figure.)

Example 2 – division estimate
  Estimate 412 ÷ 7.8
  Round: 412 ≈ 400, 7.8 ≈ 8
  400 ÷ 8
  = 50
  ≈ 50
  (Choose values that make the division easier.)

sections.title: Rounding to 1 s.f.
sections.content:
Round each number to 1 significant figure.

(a) 47
(b) 683
(c) 3.62
(d) 0.078

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 48 rounded to 1 s.f. is 50
✗ 3.7 rounded to 1 s.f. is 3
✓ Estimating gives an approximate answer, not exact
✗ 0.052 rounded to 1 s.f. is 0.1
✓ √50 ≈ 7 because 7² = 49
